lines.text: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are learning about super senses!
How do animals see, hear and smell?
Three animal friends will show us. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Get your eyes, ears and nose ready. Let's go!
Which animal can hide in the water, and still see, hear and breathe?
Is it the hippo? Or is it the horse?
It is the hippo!
Here is the fun fact. A hippo's eyes, ears and nose are all on the top of its head.
So a hippo can stay in the water, with just its eyes and nose peeking out. Peekaboo!
Two eyes, two ears, and a nose with two holes. Let's count. One, two, three!
What happens when the hippo goes all the way under the water? Hmm.
Its nose closes tight, and its ears fold down. No water gets in!
A big hippo can stay under the water for about five minutes!
And here is a surprise. Hippos do not really swim. They push off the bottom of the river, and bounce along!
When the sun goes down, the hippo comes out to munch on grass. Munch, munch, munch!
Say it with me. Eyes, ears and nose on top!
Can you peek like a hippo? Hide down low, then peek your eyes out. Peekaboo!
Now close your nose, like a hippo going under. Hold it! And let go!
Quick check! Can a hippo close its nose under the water? Yes, or no?
Yes! Its nose closes tight. Great job!
Who has a big horn on its nose?
Is it the cow? Or is it the rhino?
It is the rhino!
Here is the fun fact. A rhino cannot see very well.
But a rhino has super ears, and a super nose! It can hear and smell very, very well.
Now look at the rhino's horn. What do you think it is made of?
The same stuff as your fingernails! Look at your fingernails. Tap, tap, tap!
A rhino's horn keeps growing a little bit every year, just like your nails.
A rhino's skin is thick, with deep folds. Like a big, gray coat!
And a rhino is very, very big. The white rhino is the second biggest animal on land.
Who is the biggest? The elephant! Only the elephant is bigger than the white rhino.
A rhino has a wide, flat lip, for munching on grass. Munch, munch!
Say it with me. A rhino has a super nose!
Can you sniff like a rhino? Sniff, sniff, sniff!
Now put your hands by your ears, and listen like a rhino. Listen!
Quick check! A rhino's horn is made of the same stuff as what? Your nails? Or wood?
Your nails! Tap, tap, tap. Super thinking!
Who can hear a tiny mouse digging under the snow?
Is it the fox? Or is it the pig?
It is the fox!
Here is the fun fact. A fox has super ears! It can hear tiny animals digging under the ground, under the leaves, or under the snow.
Look at those big, pointy ears. They listen, listen, listen.
The fox hears a tiny sound under the snow. What does it do next? Hmm.
It sneaks up, jumps high, and pounces! Boing!
Now look at the fox's big, bushy tail.
The tail helps the fox balance, and it keeps the fox warm.
A grown-up fox can make about twelve different calls. Wow, that is a lot!
Baby foxes are called kits.
Kits grow up in a cozy den, and the den has a back door too!
Say it with me. A fox has super ears!
Can you pounce like a fox? Crouch down low. And jump! Boing!
Now listen, listen, like a fox. What can you hear?
Quick check! What helps the fox keep warm? Its tail? Or its ears?
Its tail! A big, bushy tail. You remembered!
Wow! We met three friends with super senses. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
Who has its eyes, ears and nose on the top of its head?
The hippo! Yes!
Whose horn is made of the same stuff as your nails?
The rhino! That's right!
Who can hear a tiny mouse under the snow?
The fox! You remembered!
You learned so many new things today.
Peek like a hippo. Sniff like a rhino. And pounce like a fox!
Which super sense is your favorite?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
